best_for: Technicians and Linux hoppers who keep a drawer of USB sticks for installers, and want one drive that boots any of their ISO files from a menu.
description:
Ventoy is a free, open-source tool for making a USB drive that can boot many operating system images from one stick. It is written by a developer who goes by longpanda and is released under the GPL-3.0.

The drive can still hold your normal files, and an ISO larger than 4 GB is no problem. You can sort images into folders and give menu entries your own names and short tips, then switch the boot menu between a flat list and a tree. Ventoy can run a Windows or Linux setup on its own from an answer script, so you can install the same system on many PCs without clicking through each one. When a new Linux release comes out, you just copy the new ISO; Ventoy does not need an update.

points.title: Copy the ISO and boot
points.text: After a one-time setup, you copy ISO, WIM, IMG, VHD(x) or EFI files onto the drive and pick one from a menu at boot. There is no re-flashing per image, and the project says more than 1,400 images have been tested.

points.title: Setup erases the drive
points.text: The first install formats the USB drive and deletes everything on it. Later updates keep the files on the first partition, so only the initial run is destructive. Back up the stick before you start.

points.title: Secure Boot takes a one-time step
points.text: Secure Boot support is a checkbox in `Ventoy2Disk.exe`. On first boot you enroll a key in the blue MOK screen, once per computer. Some PCs also need the Microsoft third-party UEFI CA enabled, and on machines where it fails, you turn Secure Boot off.

points.title: Wide firmware and filesystem support
points.text: It boots on Legacy BIOS and on IA32, x86_64, ARM64 and MIPS64EL UEFI. The data partition can be exFAT, NTFS, FAT32, UDF, XFS, Btrfs or ext2/3/4, and Linux persistence files are supported.

points.title: A zip, not an installer
points.text: The Windows download is a zip in x86, x64, ARM and ARM64 builds; you unzip it and run the tool. This site keeps 21 Windows versions. Linux users get a separate package from the Ventoy site with a GUI and a `Ventoy2Disk.sh` script.
